request: The quotes API is too slow at checkout. Make it fast. It belongs under Feature #80 (Partner integrations).

exchanges.say: You want quotes to be fast at checkout. Two words to unpack: "slow" and "fast" say nothing about which call, what number, or under what load. The API has POST /quotes and GET /quotes/{id} (route:/quotes, route:/quotes/{id}), and nothing measures it yet (gap:api-budget). Four questions, riskiest first.

questions.ask: Which call must be fast? The API has POST /quotes and GET /quotes/{id} (route:/quotes, route:/quotes/{id}); I'd guess POST /quotes at checkout.
questions.default: POST /quotes, from request sent to quote received, because that is what partners wait on.

questions.ask: What number must it meet, at which percentile? Nothing is measured here yet: there is no load test or API budget (gap:api-budget).
questions.default: p95, with your number, because most partners' customers must not wait.

questions.ask: Under what load: how many quotes a second at peak, and how many parcels in each?
Must every quote amount stay exactly as it is today? Each parcel is priced in turn today (code:src/routes/quotes.js).

answers.text: POST /quotes, the call partner shops make at checkout. Fetching a stored quote is fine.
p95 under 300 ms for a quote of 10 parcels. Partners tell us it takes about a second today.
About 20 quotes a second at peak, each with up to 10 parcels.
The amounts must stay exactly the same; only the speed changes.

exchanges.say: So: POST /quotes, p95 under 300 ms for 10 parcels at about 20 quotes a second, with the amounts unchanged. Four more about proof and scope.

questions.ask: How should it be proven, and for how long: a load test against a local server on the seeded rate table?
questions.default: A repeatable load test on the seeded data, because a partner's checkout cannot be captured as proof.

questions.ask: Should the first request after the server starts count?
questions.default: Measure after one warm-up request, because partners call a running service.

questions.ask: Do you want a k6 budget in CI so it stays fast?
questions.default: None in this story; park it, because a CI budget is its own decision.

questions.ask: Only POST /quotes, leaving GET /quotes/{id} and the OpenAPI contract alone?

answers.text: A one-minute load test against a local server with the seeded rate table; that is what partners would feel.
Not in this story; we'll decide CI budgets separately.
Only POST /quotes. Leave GET /quotes/{id} and the contract as they are.

exchanges.say: Here is what done looks like. Goal: partner shops get a quote back fast enough at checkout. Done when: a one-minute load test on a local server with the seeded rate table, sending POST /quotes with 10 parcels at 20 a second, shows p95 under 300 ms; and quotes for the seeded parcels keep today's amounts to the penny. Checkpoints: the load test reports p95, then the amounts check passes. A CI budget and loading feedback are parked.
